page: Amazon Web Services m7i.metal-48xl is a general-purpose bare-metal server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processors. The system features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and 8-bit integer operations. This server does not include local storage or GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7i.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests and PassMark CPU scores. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidth for large blocks, though its overall PassMark memory score falls in the average tier. The hardware excels in specialized workloads, scoring in the top 10% for software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations. Single-core performance is moderate, ranking in the top 25% for Geekbench single-core and average for stress-ng single-core tests.

Given its high core density and memory bandwidth, this bare-metal instance is suited for large-scale multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, and database operations, as evidenced by its top-tier Redis SET performance of 192.93 million operations per second. It also supports LLM inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds for medium-sized models and top-tier prompt processing speeds for large models. The absence of local storage requires external network storage integration, which is a key architectural tradeoff. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal configuration offers high resource density and dedicated hardware access, making it a viable option for consolidation of enterprise workloads without hypervisor overhead.
